explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. `cyc W₀` is the library's own abbreviation for the ℂ-span of the right translates `g ↦ W₀ (g * h)`. The theorem says this span is closed under right translation. Mathlib has the general pieces. `Submodule.apply_mem_span_image_of_mem_span` says that applying a linear map to an element of a span gives an element of the span of the image. Right translation could be written as the linear map `LinearMap.funLeft ℂ ℂ (· * h)`. `Submodule.span_mono` would then finish the job. However, that route chains several lemmas and needs its own proof that the image of the set of translates lies inside that set (using associativity, `h * h'`). That is more than a one-lemma instantiation. I also looked for representation-theoretic lemmas on spans of translates being invariant and found none in Mathlib for this setting. The content comes from the library's own definition of `cyc`, together with routine span induction.
